eval_feedback: The two adapted-SKILL rules both landed and fixed run-1's decisive miss without any regression. Rule 1 (requester-answerable-axes-first under limited authority): R1.Q2 asked the load-bearing 'what access do the staff need' axis — the single spec-defining question the proxy CAN answer — and the user answered 통계·주문·공지 허용 / 환불 차단, capturing the core goal as a traceable Decision. This directly reverses run-1, where that axis was never asked and the core-goal assertion FAILED. Rule 2 (greenfield/territory write-path probing): the interview probed how staff accounts and roles get created (R1.Q3), discovered via territory that no non-owner login route exists (R2.Q1), and carried that as an honest Still Open build blocker — turning a silent gap into a named, owner/dev-routed unknown. Everything run-1 already did well is preserved: proxy/authority handling is textbook (owner-policy axes → pending-owner assumptions, only within-authority items in Decisions), the dormant users.role column and refund irreversibility are territory-anchored and verified, three real unknown-unknowns land (audit log, auth blocker, order PII), and no fabrication. The CAPPED tag is correctly applied and — unlike run-1 — externally forced by owner authority plus the auth blocker rather than self-inflicted by budget mismanagement, since the core was already captured in R1. 15/15 assertions, rubric 10/10 (D1 and D4 both recover from run-1's 1s). Note: the resuming/finishing invocation correctly trusted the state file over a stale prompt template and refused to overwrite answered rounds — honest lifecycle handling, no fabricated extra round.
